questions.question_text: Of all reported parasomnias, the one that is more common in females than males is
questions.explanation:
Women report nightmares more frequently, in a ratio of 2-4:1. Among children, sleep terror disorder is more prevalent in males than in
females, but in adults, the ratio is even. REM sleep behaviour disorder is more prevalent in males. Sleepwalking disorder and restless leg
syndrome have an equal sex distribution.

questions.question_text: On corneal examination, Kayser-Fleischer rings are usually present in patients with
questions.explanation:
Wilson's disease: Personality disturbances, mood abnormalities, and cognitive dysfunction being the most common psychiatric symptoms.
Kayser-Fleischer rings (copper deposits on Descemet's membrane of the cornea) are present in 95% of patients with neurological symptoms,
in 50-60% of patients without neurological symptoms and in only 10% of asymptomatic siblings. 50% of patients will have mental
disturbances at some point during the course of the disease. Psychiatric manifestations tend to occur with neurological forms of WD rather
than with hepatic ones. Speci�c treatment of WD is with copper chelating or copper depleting agents. Most neurological and psychiatric
manifestations of WD can improve with this treatment; however, the early diagnosis and initiation of the treatment is essential
(Neuropsychiatry of the basal ganglia -- Ring and Serra ..,  (accessed June 08, 2015).)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is preserved in apperceptive visual agnosia?
questions.explanation:
Visual agnosia refers to defective recognition of stimulus presented visually despite the intact sensory system. Lissauer classi�ed this into 1.
Apperceptive visual agnosia and 2. Associative visual agnosia on the basis of a two-stage model of recognition. In the former, the patient
never achieves a complete visual percept while, in the latter, such percept is formed but could not be associated with its semantic meaning.
Hence in apperceptive agnosia, drawing of objects, writing one's name and copying diagrams are preserved. Patients fail tests such as visual
matching, discriminating shapes, comparing similar �gures and copying drawings. Tests for apperceptive agnosia include object decision test
and incomplete letters test from the Visual Orientation and Space Perception Battery (VOSP). Associative visual agnosia is usually the result
of bilateral damage to the inferior temporo-occipital junction and subjacent white matter. The cause is most often infarction of the posterior
cerebral artery bilaterally. It is more common than apperceptive visual agnosia. Shelton PA et al. (1994) Apperceptive Visual Agnosia: A Case
Study. Brain and Cognition, 25(1), 1-23.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tremors increase during intentional movement?
questions.explanation:
Tremors triggered by rest are called resting tremors. Tremors triggered or made worse by movement are called action tremors. Action
tremors can be classi�ed as intention tremors (triggered by aiming for a target) or postural tremors (triggered by holding a limb in one
position). Most parkinsonian tremors are resting tremors: they are less pronounced on initiating movement. Myoclonus is not a tremor in a
strict sense.

questions.question_text:
A 76-year-old man was brought to the emergency unit by his wife. He had breakfast that morning and appeared unable to remember that
he and his wife have planned a day out. He repeatedly enquired where she was taking him. She reports that he appeared bewildered, but
was alert and had no sensory and motor de�cits throughout. He returned to a normal mental state after 10 hours. What is the most likely
diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Transient global amnesia (TGA) refers to an episode of complete and reversible anterograde and retrograde memory loss lasting up to 24 h.
Patients have a persistent loss of memory for the time of the attack. During the episode, patients often appear bewildered and ask repeated
questions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is contraindicated in angle closure glaucoma?
questions.explanation: Topiramate can increase intraocular pressure and can cause acute precipitation of angle closure glaucoma.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has the best available evidence for the treatment of depression that follows a myocardial infarction?
questions.explanation:
The Sertraline Antidepressant Heart Attack Randomized Trial (SADHART) is to date the largest randomized trial evaluating use of
antidepressant medication for depressed patients with heart disease. Sertraline vs. placebo 16-week trial, no di�erence in safety (change in
left ventricular ejection fraction, increase in premature ventricular contractions, or prolongation of the QT interval) between the treatment
and placebo groups. A nonsigni�cant reduction in the composite end point (MI or CHD death) in the sertraline group (relative risk, 0.77; 95%
con�dence interval, 0.51-1.16). SSRIs may be directly cardioprotective by reducing platelet activation. But there was little di�erence in
depression status between groups receiving sertraline and placebo after 24 weeks of treatment. However, the e�ect of sertraline was
greater in the patients with severe and recurrent depression. Ref: van Melle, J.P. et al (2007) E�ects of antidepressant treatment on long-
term depression status and cardiac prognosis in depressed MI patients. British Journal of Psychiatry, 190, 460-466.

questions.question_text: What is the risk of depression in a cardiac patient with congestive heart failure compared to the general population?
questions.explanation:
The prevalence rates of clinically signi�cant depression among CHF patients is approximately 21.5%, determined using meta-analytic tests.
Thus, the risk of clinical depression in CHF is 2 to 3 times the rate of the general population. Rutledge, T., et al. (2006). Depression in Heart
Failure: A Meta-Analytic Review of Prevalence, Intervention E�ects, and Associations with Clinical Outcomes. J Am Coll Cardiol, 48(8), 1527-
1537

questions.question_text: The mean age of onset of chronic fatigue syndrome is between
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome is nearly 0.5% with a higher rate in women [M-F - 1:3], those belonging to lower occupational
status and educational background. The mean age of onset is between 29-35 years. Mean illness duration is 3-9 years. The prevalence
seems to be lower among children and adolescents.

questions.question_text: The ratio of prevalence of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome in males compared to females is
questions.explanation:
The prevalence of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome is nearly 0.5% with a higher rate in women [M-F - 1:3], those belonging to lower occupational
status and educational background. The mean age of onset is between 29-35 years. Mean illness duration is 3-9 years. The prevalence
seems to be lower among children and adolescents.

questions.question_text: Diagnostic features of neurasthenia include the following except:
questions.explanation:
The ICD-10 diagnostic criteria for neurasthenia falls under 'Neurotic, stress-related and somatoform disorders'. The diagnostic criteria for
neurasthenia are: a. either, persistent and distressing feelings of exhaustion after minor mental e�ort or persistent and distressing feelings
of fatigue after minor physical e�ort; b. accompanied by one or more of the following symptoms: muscular aches or pains; dizziness; tension
headache; sleep disturbance; inability to relax; and irritability; c. inability to recover through rest, relaxation or enjoyment; d. duration
exceeds 3 months; e. Does not occur in the presence of organic mental disorders, a�ective disorders or panic or generalised anxiety
disorder. (Excerpt from Hickie, L., Davenport, T., Issakidis, C., et al. (2002) Neurasthenia: prevalence, disability and health care characteristics
in the Australian community. British Journal of Psychiatry, 181, 56-61).

questions.question_text:
A 42-year-old woman presents with a history of 2 episodes of unilateral blindness that lasted for few weeks. Now she has paraesthesia of
left leg and MRI shows multiple demyelinating plaques. Which of the following with regard to her illness is correct?

options.text: It has a uniform progressive course.
It is due to a bacterial infection
It presents with diverse physical signs
It is more common in men than women
Occurs more commonly nearer the equator

correct_answer.text: It presents with diverse physical signs

questions.explanation:
The description is suggestive of multiple sclerosis. In the UK, the lifetime risk is 1:8000; It is twice as common in women as in men and is
seen with greater frequency as the distance from the equator increases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms are not indicative of chronic fatigue syndrome?
questions.explanation:
The core symptom of CFS is fatigue. However, pain and cognitive di�culties can be as prominent as fatigue. Almost all patients develop
functional impairment. According to NICE, symptoms that might indicate another serious illness include signi�cant weight loss; clinically
signi�cant lymphadenopathy; localising or focal neurological signs; features of in�ammatory arthritis, connective tissue disease, or
cardiorespiratory disease; and sleep apnoea.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of sleep terror disorder?

options.text: Vivid memory of dreams on waking up

questions.explanation:
The average sleep terror episode lasts for about 15 minutes. Sleep terror is an NREM disorder - unlike nightmares, the memory of the dream
or even of arousal is poor on waking up. An increase in muscle tone with two to four-fold increase in heart rate is observed. Narcolepsy is
associated with HLA polymorphisms.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of subcortical dementia?
questions.explanation:
Sub cortical dementias include Parkinson's disease dementia, Huntington's disease, HIV-associated dementia, Binswanger's disease and
Wilson's disease. Subcortical dementias are characterised by gross psychomotor slowing, abnormal movements, low mood, mild amnesia
and apathetic personality.

Somatoform disorder: This condition is characterised by patients with chronic pain that is not caused by any physical or speci�c psychiatric
symptoms. Speci�c pain syndromes include headache, facial pain, backache and pelvic pain. Here pain is the predominant focus of
presentation. A full description of the pain and the circumstances in which it occurs should be explored. Psychological factors may have an
important role in onset, severity and exacerbation. Assessment should involve beliefs about the causes of pain and its implications, pain
behaviours including the presentation of symptoms, requests for medication and responses to pain should be explored. The pain is of
su�cient severity to cause distress or impairment of social and occupational functioning.

questions.question_text: A cognitive faculty most often a�ected in patients with post concussion syndrome is
questions.explanation: processing speed is the most a�ected - correlates with severity of symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms occur commonly in patients with postconcussional syndrome?

options.text: Short term memory loss and personality changes
Dizziness, headaches, irritability, slowed mental process

correct_answer.text: Dizziness, headaches, irritability, slowed mental process

questions.explanation:
Post concussional syndrome is the commonest psychiatric disorder following head injury. It occurs following head trauma, usually
su�ciently severe to result in loss of consciousness. Since this syndrome often occurs after mild head injury, it has been suggested that it is
psychologically based. The duration and severity of symptoms are highly variable. The symptoms would include headache, fatigue, dizziness,
irritability, increased sensitivity to noise, anxiety, depression, mild cognitive impairment leading to impairment of memory, insomnia, sleep
disturbance, reduced tolerance to stress and possibly sexual dysfunction. It is also accompanied by feelings of anxiety or depression,
resulting from loss of self-esteem and fear of permanent brain damage and hypochondriacal symptoms are not uncommon. Some of them
embark on a search for diagnosis and cure and may adopt a permanent sick role. These complaints are not necessarily associated with
compensation motives. It generally resolves following mild or moderate head injury but persists inde�nitely in a small proportion of patients
with severe head injury

questions.question_text:
A patient had a stroke 8 months ago. He now presents with apathy, amotivation and anhedonia. He does not have any tearfulness or
pessimism. His MMSE score is 22/30 and he has dysexecutive function. What is his most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Patients who have vascular depression have more apathy, retardation, less depressive thinking such as guilt and worthlessness, poor
executive function on cognitive testing, than do elderly individuals who are depressed without vascular risk factors.

questions.question_text:
A 29-year-old woman, who is 6 months pregnant, is referred to your clinic for an opinion. She is depressed, has a previous history of
depression and a family history of depression. She has responded well to paroxetine in the past. If she were to continue with Paroxetine
throughout pregnancy, which of the following e�ects is most likely to be seen in the newborn?
questions.explanation:
Paroxetine, particularly high-dose �rst trimesters exposure, is clearly linked to cardiac malformation - VSD and ASD. Third trimester use can
give rise to neonatal complication such as irritability due to abrupt withdrawals. Risk of neonatal withdrawal symptoms is high with
paroxetine due to short half life

questions.question_text: An antidepressant with best evidence for use in post stroke depression is
questions.explanation:
Nortriptyline is a second-generation tricyclic antidepressant. Patients with cardiovascular disease should be given nortriptyline only under
close supervision because of the tendency of the drug to produce tachycardia and to prolong the conduction time (QT) like most other
tricyclics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pregnant mothers have the highest risk of having a child with ADHD?

options.text: 30 year old lady who drinks one glass of red wine a day
31 year old lady who drinks 3 mugs of co�ee a day
21 year old lady who smokes 12 'roll-up' cigarettes a day
26 year old lady who has no substance use habits
22 year old lady who smokes one joint of marijuana a day

correct_answer.text: 21 year old lady who smokes 12 'roll-up' cigarettes a day

questions.explanation: Nicotine exposure in pregnancy is increasingly being associated with the risk of ADHD in children.

questions.question_text:
A 21-year-old woman has been diagnosed with postnatal depression and is currently receiving antidepressant treatment. Which observer
rating would be most appropriate to use, to assess her response to treatment?
questions.explanation:
Montgomery Asberg depression rating scale (MADRS) is a 10 items version, which is most sensitive to change when measuring the severity
of depression. It requires a clinical interview similar to Hamilton depression rating scale. Zung rating scale is insensitive to change. Beck
depression scale is a self rating scale with 21 item, which lacks discriminatory power for the severely ill.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct with regard to the mechanism of action of moda�nil?
questions.explanation:
Moda�nil's exact mechanism of action is still not known, but it exhibits selectivity for hypothalamic arousal systems and has been shown to
activate orexin neurons in rodents. Numerous in vitro studies have shown it to increase the levels of various monoamines, namely;
dopamine in the striatum and nucleus accumbens, noradrenaline in the hypothalamus, and serotonin in the amygdala and frontal cortex.
Moda�nil activates glutamatergic circuits while inhibiting GABAergic neurotransmission.

questions.question_text: Moda�nil, which is used for daytime sleepiness, causes which of the following neurochemical changes?
questions.explanation:
Moda�nil, like other stimulants, increases the release of monoamines speci�cally the catecholamines, norepinephrine and dopamine from
the synaptic terminals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common side e�ect of moda�nil?
questions.explanation:
Moda�nil was originally indicated for narcolepsy, but has been recently approved by the FDA (USA) for treatment of ADHD in children. Its
mechanism of action is thought to be through di�use cortical activation via adrenergic systems as well as through thalamic and reticular
activation system attenuation. It also has a low abuse potential. It has an e�ect size of 0.7 after titration to a full dose after 7 to 9 days, to an
average dose of 300 to 400 mg/day. Side e�ects are headache, appetite suppression, nervousness, and sleep disturbance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants has an e�ect in common with anti-nausea drugs such as ondansetron?
questions.explanation:
Mirtazapine can block 5HT3 receptors similar to the anti-nausea drugs ondansetron used in cancer chemotherapy. Due to this e�ect the
side e�ect of nausea is very low with mirtazapine.

questions.question_text:
A 30-year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder is currently breastfeeding her child.  She has a manic relapse, though the
presentation is not severe enough to warrant hospitalisation. What would be the best medication to treat her relapse?
questions.explanation:
Maudsley prescribing guidelines advises us to refrain from using any mood stabilisers if at all possible in breast feeding mothers. If
necessary one may use valproate. Treatment of bipolar disorder invariably requires mood stabilizers, lorazepam and chloral hydrate can be
safely excluded. Maternal use of lithium and carbamazepine has been associated with serious di�culties in babies. Lithium increases the
risk of thyroid dysfunction, cyanosis, poor muscle tone, and ECG changes in infants. Also renal clearance is decreased in infants up to at
least 5 months of age, so the use of lithium during breastfeeding is not advisable unless the mother was already on lithium and
discontinuation led to severe relapse not treatable by any other drug. In this case both infant and mother's lithium levels need monitoring.
There has been a single recorded case of serious blood abnormalities following exposure to sodium valproate through breast milk, and
hepatotoxicity can occur when valproate is directly administered to infants. Therefore, when administering valproate to breastfeeding
mothers, pediatric clinical status, liver enzymes, and platelets should be carefully monitored. Carbamazepine can cause hepatic dysfunction
and so it is advisable to monitor liver enzymes, bilirubin, and WBC counts frequently and to assay for carbamazepine levels in exposed
infants. There is limited, though reassuring data on lamotrigine and no data for the use of gabapentin by nursing mothers. But these agents
are not �rst-line medications for bipolar disorder. Burt et al. (2001) The use of psychotropic medication during breastfeeding. Am J
Psychiatry 158:1001-1009.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic symptom of hepatic encephalopathy?
questions.explanation: Liver �ap is seen in hepatic failure associated with encephalopathic state.

questions.question_text:
A 45-year-old woman comes to see you with her husband. He is concerned about her behaviour - she seems on a constant high and has
spent a lot of their money on shopping sprees. She is completely unconcerned about that but is worried about a rash on her face and tells
you that she has had several mouth ulcers recently. The rash on her face gets worse on sunny days. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: It is important to note that SLE can present as camou�aged bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following modes of psychotherapy has established evidence in HIV associated depression?
questions.explanation:
Interpersonal therapy has established evidence in HIV related depression. Markowitz JC, et al. Treatment of depressive symptoms in human
immunode�ciency virus-positive patients. Arch Gen Psychiatry. 1998;55:452-457.

questions.question_text: A man presents with drooping of the left lip and inability to fully close his left eye though he can frown. What is the likely cause of the lesion?

options.text: Facial nerve palsy (upper motor neuron type)
Facial nerve palsy(lower motor neuron type)

correct_answer.text: Facial nerve palsy (upper motor neuron type)

questions.explanation:
In UMN palsy of facial nerve, the upper part of face is spared. This is because the forehead muscles receive input from both ipsilateral and
contralateral higher cortical centres.

questions.question_text: In which of the following neurological conditions anaemia is a common �nding?
questions.explanation:
In subacute combined degeneration of cord (SACD), vitamin B12 de�ciency produces spinal degeneration, peripheral neuropathy and
macrocytic anaemia. The most common cause is pernicious anaemia, an autoimmune condition.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of comorbid depression in those with coronary heart disease is
questions.explanation:
In patients with CHD, the prevalence of major depression is nearly 20%, and the prevalence of a minor depressive disorder is approximately
27%. When present in patients with existing CHD, depression is independently associated with worse outcome, including higher morbidity
and mortality, and worse health status (Depression and CHD risk: How should we intervene? - Springer. Retrieved from

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about suicide rates in patients with Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation:
In Huntington's disease, the risk of suicide is 4 times higher than the general population. This increased risk is also seen in una�ected
individuals in the same family. One must be careful not to o�er insensitive or uninformed genetic counselling to the family.

questions.question_text: Amnesia is the most common residual de�cit following recovery from
questions.explanation: Herpes simplex encephalitis a�ects temporal lobes resulting in residual amnesia that may persist after recovery from the acute infection.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs in Ganser's syndrome?

options.text: Disorientation in time, place and person

questions.explanation:
Ganser's syndrome is a rare syndrome characterized by approximate answers, clouded consciousness, pseudo-hallucinations and hysterical
conversion symptoms. The symptom of approximate answers is more common than the syndrome. The complete syndrome is very rare.

questions.question_text:
A patient known to have bipolar disorder with mixed a�ective state is in the �rst trimester of her pregnancy. She has not been on any
medications of late. What would you prescribe to her?
questions.explanation:
"For women who have had a long period without relapse, the possibilities of withdrawing treatment before conception and for at least the
�rst trimester should be considered". (Maudsley.2007). Avoid combination of mood stabilizers. Valproate has good evidence in mixed
a�ective state but not preferred during �rst trimester, olanzapine may be safer. If valproate is prescribe, prophylactic folic acid (5 mg daily,
from at least a month before conception) should be used. Prophylactic Vitamin K should also be given to both the mother and the neonate
after delivery if valproate is used during pregnancy.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following medications could be used to treat pathological crying?
questions.explanation:
For pathological crying, �uoxetine and sertraline have been evaluated in small parallel RCTs with favourable results; citalopram in a cross
over trial showed signi�cant bene�ts and fewer side-e�ects

questions.question_text: A pregnant bipolar patient has no other treatment option but to continue valproate. Which of the following should she take in addition?
questions.explanation: Folate supplements reduce the risk of neural tube defects

questions.question_text: What would be the most appropriate drug for a depressed lady who is pregnant?
questions.explanation:
Fluoxetine has the most evidence and is safer than paroxetine. Other drugs recommended by Maudlsey guidelines include Amitryptyline,
Nortryptyline and Imipramine. (Maudsley guidelines- 10th edition pg 354)

questions.question_text: Which of the following points towards dissociative pseudoseizures rather than epileptic seizures?

options.text: Total duration being less than 30 secs

questions.explanation:
Features which are common in pseudoseizures but rarer in epilepsy include: biting the tip of the tongue, seizures lasting more than 2
minutes, seizures having a gradual onset, a �uctuating course of disease severity, the eyes being closed during a seizure, and side to side
head movements.

questions.question_text: Idiopathic progressive calcium deposition in the basal ganglia is seen in
questions.explanation:
Fahr's disease is caused due to idiopathic progressive calcium deposition in the basal ganglia. Onset between the ages of 20 and 40 is
associated with schizophreniform psychoses and catatonic symptoms. Onset between the ages of 40 and 60 has been associated with
dementia and choreoathetosis. Depression is also very common. 50% had psychiatric problems and psychiatric symptoms correlate with
more extensive calci�cation. The pattern of cognitive impairment found in FD is of the frontosubcortical type.

questions.question_text: Presence of which of the following will prompt investigations for a medical cause of recurrent anxiety?

options.text: Onset of symptoms before the age of 25 years

questions.explanation:
Factors that imply an organic aetiology for anxiety include - onset of symptoms after the age of 35 years, lack of anticipatory anxiety, lack of
avoidance behavior, and lack of personal or family history of anxiety disorders and poor response to short term anxiolytics

questions.question_text: What percentage of women with postpartum psychosis will go on to develop schizophrenia later in their lifetime?
questions.explanation:
Explanation: Diagnostically, most patients with postpartum psychosis later receive a diagnosis of a�ective disorder; schizophrenia is
diagnosed in around 16%. The overall prognosis was good, except for schizophrenia, in which more than 50% of patients had chronic
disability.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms do you see more often in the later rather than the early stages of HIV dementia?
questions.explanation: Except paraparesis, other symptoms are seen even in early stages of HIV dementia.

questions.question_text: Most common psychiatric symptom in Cushing's syndrome is
questions.explanation:
Cushing's syndrome, the result of an excess of corticosteroid, is very frequently, although not invariably, associated with depression. This
association was observed even with the earliest case descriptions of this endocrine disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following MRI �nding is characteristically seen in Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation:
Caudate atrophy with box-car ventricles is noted in Huntington's. Knife blade gyri are seen in Pick's disease. Multiple white matter
hyperintensities are seen in vascular dementia and age-related changes. Pulvinar sign is seen in variant CJD.

questions.question_text:
Mr. Y has been treated for multiple sclerosis, and he developed depression following treatment. Which of the following drugs is most likely
to have induced the depression?
questions.explanation:
Beta and alpha interferons used in the treatment of multiple sclerosis is associated with depression. The role of beta interferons in the
etiology of Multiple Sclerosis related depression is unclear. Standard care for initiation of beta interferon should include assessment for
depression and for those with a past history of depressive illness, prophylactic treatment with an antidepressant is recommended (Ref: The
Maudsley prescribing guidelines; 10th edition; pg 410)

questions.question_text:
A 45-year-old diabetic gentleman was brought to the emergency department with nausea, vomiting, lethargy and muscle cramps. He has
been diagnosed with depression and has been started on �uoxetine recently. What is the most likely metabolic complication?
questions.explanation: All antidepressants can cause hyponatremia, especially SSRIs like Fluoxetine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an e�ective treatment for post-stroke depression based on the best available evidence?
questions.explanation:
A metaanalysis that pooled 385 patients from 6 trials published through December 2009 that evaluated the prophylactic e�cacy of
�uoxetine in poststroke patients. They found that �uoxetine reduced the incidence of poststroke depression, helped recovery in neurologic
function, and improved independence in activities of daily living.

questions.question_text: What rating scale would you recommend to a health visitor who wants to screen for depression in women after delivery?
questions.explanation:
EPDS is a 10-item self-report scale to screen for Postnatal Depression in the community. The scale can be completed in about 5 minutes and
has a simple method of scoring that can be used by health visitors and midwivesExcerpted from Cox et al. Detection of postnatal
depression. Development of the 10-item Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. The British Journal of Psychiatry.1987; 150: 782-786.

questions.question_text: In ICD 10 which of the following is included under dissociative disorders?
questions.explanation:
.'Trance and possession' disorders are placed under the general rubric of dissociative disorder (ICD-10) implying a psychological causation of
symptoms. Possession is characterized by a transient alteration in identity whereby one's normal identity is temporarily replaced or
possessed by a spirit, ghost, deity, etc. This disorder may be culture-bound for some non-Western cultures.

questions.question_text: What is the case fatality rate in patients with herpes simplex encephalitis?
questions.explanation:
Untreated, there is a case fatality of ~70% for Herpes simplex encephalitis. Treatment with intravenous aciclovir reduces fatality to 20-30%.
Treatment in proven cases should continue for at least 14 days, longer in immunocompromised patients

questions.question_text: During the psychiatric consultation, Mr. Y says 'I feel like a woman trapped in a man's body'. This describes a core clinical feature seen in
questions.explanation:
Transsexualism is characterized by the feeling of one's gender being di�erent from one's biological sex. "These patients have an enduring
belief that they are really of the opposite sex. This is associated with marked unhappiness and discomfort in the birth sex and a persistent
desire to live and be treated as a member of the opposite sex Transvestism (the wearing of clothes of the opposite sex for sexual or other
purposes, not associated with the core belief of incorrect gender found in the transsexual)

questions.question_text:
A 33 year old man has intractable seizures. Which of the following factors may support a diagnosis of non-epileptic seizures rather than true
epilepsy?

options.text: Less likely to maintain body tone during a seizure
More likely to sustain injury from seizures

questions.explanation:
The following factors in the history may support a diagnosis of non-epileptic seizures. (Dilley and Fleminger, 2006) 1. A psychiatric history 2.
Regaining alertness and orientation rapidly 3. Ability to recall events clearly 4. The presence of social stressors.

questions.question_text: As regards drug therapy in palliative care all are true except

options.text: Amitryptyline is useful for neuropathic pain
SSRIs have well established evidence base for depression in palliative care
Tricyclics may produce troublesome side e�ects and delirium.
Lorazepam is useful for acute anxiety
Risperidone may be useful for psychotic symptoms in terminally ill patients

correct_answer.text: SSRIs have well established evidence base for depression in palliative care

questions.explanation:
The evidence base for treating various psychiatric symptoms in palliative care is feeble; the use of SSRIs is empirical rather than evidence-
based.

questions.question_text: MRI shows hypointensity of striatum in patients with
questions.explanation:
The commonest neurological features of FD are Parkinsonism, chorea, dystonia, tremor, gait disturbance, dysarthria, seizures, and
myoclonus. Fahr's syndrome - speci�c causes of calcium deposition in the basal ganglia such as hypoparathyroidism. Radiological basal
ganglia calci�cation without clinical features on CT may occur at a rate of about 0.9% of cases. MRI shows hypointensity of the striatum. EEG
is non-speci�c - may show di�use changes

questions.question_text: 'Baby blues' are reported in what proportion of new mothers?
questions.explanation:
Baby blues: Up to 3/4 of new mothers will experience a short-lived period of tearfulness and emotional lability starting two or three days
after birth and lasting one to two days. This is common enough to be easily recognizable by midwifery sta� and requires only reassurance
and observation towards resolution. There is weak evidence that it may be related to post-partum reductions in levels of oestrogen,
progesterone, and prolactin (which do occur around 72 hrs after the birth). Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 756

questions.question_text: Doctor-shopping is an entity associated with which psychiatric condition?
questions.explanation:
Somatisation disorder: "Diagnosis is usually only suspected after negative �ndings begin to emerge as normal medical practice is to take
complaints at face value. Key diagnostic feature is multiple, atypical, and inconsistent medically unexplained symptoms in a patient under
the age of 40. There is excessive use of medical service and alternative therapies. Chronic cases will have had large numbers of diagnostic
procedures and surgical or medical treatments. High risk of iatrogenic harm and iatrogenic substance dependence. Hostility and frustration
can be felt on both sides of the doctor-patient relationship. There may be doctor-shopping and splitting of the attitudes of sta� caring for
them. Psychological approaches to treatment are hampered by on-going investigations of ever rarer diagnostic possibilities and by the
attribution of symptoms to �ctitious but named medical entities". (Excerpt from Oxford Handbook of Psychiatry; 744)

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect about somatisation disorder?

options.text: Most frequent symptoms are non speci�c and atypical

questions.question_text: What percentage of patients will die by completed suicide in the 12 months after an initial parasuicidal act?
questions.explanation:
Risk of suicide within one year of DSH - 0.7% (nearly 1 in 100); more in males 1.1%; 0.5% in females. This is 66 x the general population risk.
Roughly 1% will die by completed suicide in the 24 months after the initial parasuicidal act, with the risk highest in the weeks following the
original act. This represents mortality by suicide 50-100 times that of the general population. Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 730

questions.explanation:
Risk factors for completed suicide Socio-demographic factors: Male sex, Elderly, Single, divorced, or widowed, Living alone, poor social
support, Unemployed or low socio-economic class Personal/mental health factors: Previous Parasuicide or DSH, Any mental disorder
(greatest risk in major depression and anorexia nervosa, then functional psychosis, then neurotic and personality disorders), Dependence
on alcohol or drugs, Recent inpatient psychiatric treatment, Concurrent physical disorder and Recent bereavement

questions.question_text: The peak incidence of head injury is between the ages of
questions.explanation:
Peak incidence of head injury is between the ages of 15 - 24 years. Concussion damage causes transient coma for hours followed by
apparent complete clinical recovery. Brain contusion leads to prolonged coma, focal signs and lasting brain damage.

questions.question_text: The most common co-morbid psychiatric condition associated with hypochondriasis is
questions.explanation:
Patients with hypochondriasis have a high rate of psychiatric comorbidity. In one outpatient clinical series, 88% of patients with
hypochondriasis had one or more concurrent psychiatric disorders, the most common being generalized anxiety disorder (71%), dysthymic
disorder (45.2%), major depression (42.9%), somatization disorder (21.4%), and panic disorder (16.7%). These patients are 3 times more
likely to have a personality disorder than the general population. Arch Gen Psychiatry. Feb 1992;49(2):101-8.

Moclobemide is not known to be pro-convulsive and is a good choice. SSRIs are considered to be a good choice too in epileptic patients.
Most TCAs are epileptogenic and ideally should be avoided completely. Amitriptyline, Dothiepin, Clomipramine and Bupropion should be

In children older than 3 months and in adults, HSE is usually localized to the temporal and frontal lobes and is caused by herpes simplex
